```{r functions, eval=T, echo=F}
gl.subsample.ind2 <- function (x, n = NULL, replace = TRUE, by.pop = TRUE, error.check = TRUE, mono.rm = FALSE, verbose = NULL)
{
  if (error.check == TRUE) {
    verbose <- gl.check.verbosity(verbose)
    funname <- match.call()[[1]]
    utils.flag.start(func = funname, build = "v.2023.3", 
                     verbose = verbose)
    datatype <- utils.check.datatype(x, verbose = verbose)
    if (!is(x, "dartR")) {
      class(x) <- "dartR"
      if (verbose > 2) {
        cat("Warning: Standard adegenet genlight object encountered. Converted to compatible dartR genlight object\n")
        cat("                    Should you wish to convert it back to an adegenet genlight object for later use outside dartR, \n                 please use function dartR2gl\n")
      }
    }
    if (n < 1) {
      cat(error("Fatal Error: Number of individuals must be a positive integer\n"))
      stop()
    }
    n.limit <- min(table(pop(x)))
    if (is.null(n)) {
      if (by.pop) {
        n <- n.limit
      }
      else {
        n <- nInd(x)
      }
    }
    if (by.pop == TRUE) {
      if (n > n.limit) {
        if (verbose >= 1) {
          cat("  Warning: Specified subsample size larger than smallest population size\n")
        }
        if (replace == FALSE) {
          if (verbose >= 1) {
            cat("    Sampling without replacement, n set to", 
                n.limit, "\n Only populations larger than n will be  subsampled\n")
          }
          #n <- n.limit
        }
        else {
          if (verbose >= 1) {
            cat("    Some populations will be upsampled by replacement\n")
          }
        }
      }
    }
    if (by.pop == FALSE) {
      if (n > nLoc(x)) {
        if (verbose >= 1) {
          cat("  Warning: Specified subsample size larger than total number of individuals\n")
        }
        if (replace == FALSE) {
          if (verbose >= 1) {
            cat("    Sampling without replacement, n set to", 
                nLoc(x), "\n")
          }
          n <- nLoc(x)
        }
        else {
          if (verbose >= 1) {
            cat("    Some populations will be upsampled by replacement\n")
          }
        }
        n <- nLoc(x)
      }
    }
  }
  subsample <- function(x, n, replace) {
    if (n <= nInd(x)) {
      idx <- sample(seq_len(nInd(x)), size = n, replace = replace)
      xx <- x[idx, ]
    }
    if (n > nInd(x)) {
      if (replace == TRUE) {
        idx <- sample(seq_len(nInd(x)), size = nInd(x), 
                      replace = TRUE)
        xx <- x[idx, ]
        if (n/nInd(x) >= 2) {
          for (i in 1:trunc(n/nInd(x)) - 1) {
            idx <- sample(seq_len(nInd(x)), size = nInd(x), 
                          replace = TRUE)
            tmp <- x[idx, ]
            xx <- gl.join(xx, tmp, method = "join.by.loc", 
                          verbose = 0)
          }
        }
        if (n%%nInd(x) > 0) {
          idx <- sample(seq_len(nInd(x)), size = (n%%nInd(x)), 
                        replace = TRUE)
          tmp <- x[idx, ]
          xx <- gl.join(xx, tmp, method = "join.by.loc", 
                        verbose = 0)
        }
      }
      else {
        cat("n larger than population size, no subsampling occurred\n")
        #stop()
        xx <- x
      }
    }
    return(xx)
  }
  if (by.pop == FALSE) {
    xx <- subsample(x = x, n = n, replace = replace)
  }
  if (by.pop == TRUE) {
    new.list <- list()
    pop_names <- popNames(x)
    for (i in seq_along(pop_names)) {
      gl <- gl.keep.pop(x, pop.list = pop_names[i], verbose = 0)
      new.list[[i]] <- subsample(x = gl, n = n, replace = replace)
    }
    if (length(new.list) > 1) {
      xx <- new.list[[1]]
      for (i in 2:length(new.list)) {
        xx <- gl.join(xx, new.list[[i]], method = "join.by.loc", 
                      verbose = 0)
      }
    }
    else {
      xx <- new.list[[1]]
    }
  }
  if (error.check == TRUE) {
    if (mono.rm == TRUE) {
      x <- gl.filter.monomorphs(x, verbose = verbose)
      nh <- length(x2@other$history)
      x2@other$history[[nh + 1]] <- match.call()
    }
    if (verbose >= 1) {
      cat("Completed:", funname, "\n")
    }
  }
  return(xx)
}


gl.opt.ind.all <- function(x, first="optimal", plot=FALSE, bootstrap=NULL, ncores=1, percent=0.95)
{
  
  #nnet function which is max (helper function)
  which.is.max <- function (x)
  {
    y <- seq_along(x)[x == max(x)]
    if (length(y) > 1L)
      sample(y, 1L)
    else y
  }
  
  xx <- as.matrix(x) # convert to matrix
  colnames(xx) <- rownames(x) <- NULL
  
  optind<- function(xx, indnr=NULL) {
    orderind<-NA
    nalltot <- NA
    
    for (i in 1:nInd(x))
    {
      nall_ind <- rowSums((xx %% 2)+1, na.rm=TRUE) # count the number of alleles per individuals)
      nextind <- which.is.max(nall_ind) # find the individual with the most alleles
      if (i==1 & first=="random") nextind <- sample(1:nInd(x), 1) # if first individual, select a random one
      if (i==1 && first=="all" ) nextind <- indnr
      #remove loci and individuals with the most alleles
      all_ind <- xx[nextind,]
      xx[nextind,]<- NA
      xx[,all_ind==1]<- NA
      # for (a in 1:nrow(xx)) {
      #    for(b in 1:ncol(xx)) {
      #     if (!is.na(all_ind[b]) && !is.na(xx[a,b])) {
      #    if (xx[a,b]== 1) xx[a,b] <- 2-all_ind[b]  else  if (xx[a,b] == all_ind[b]) xx[a,b] <- NA
      #    }
      # }
      #}
      
      for (ii in 1:ncol(xx)) {
        if (!is.na(all_ind[ii])) {
          xx[xx[,ii] ==all_ind[ii],ii] <- NA # remove the alleles of the individual with the most alleles
          
          xx[xx[,ii]==1,ii] <- 2-all_ind[ii] # convert heterozygotes to homozygotes
        }
      }
      orderind[i] <- nextind
      nalltot[i] <- nall_ind[nextind] # number of alleles added by individual
      if (sum(is.na(xx)) == ncol(xx) * nrow(xx)) break # stop if all alleles are removed
      # if (i %% 10 ==0) cat(paste("individual", i, "\n")); flush.console() # print progress every 10 individuals
    }
    return(list(orderind=orderind, nalltot=nalltot))
  }
  
  
  if (first=="optimal") {
    res <- optind(xx)
    df <- data.frame(order=res$orderind, id=indNames(x)[res$orderind], pop=pop(x)[res$orderind],nall=cumsum(res$nalltot), nallperc =  round(cumsum(res$nalltot)/sum(res$nalltot),3) )
    if (plot) {
      p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x=1:nrow(df), y=nallperc, col=pop))+geom_point()+xlab("individual")+ylab("percent alleles retained")+ylim(c(0.5,1))
      print(p1)
    }
  }
  else {
    
    plan(multisession, workers=ncores)
    if (first=="all") bootstrap=nInd(x)
    df <- future_sapply(1:bootstrap, FUN=function(i) optind(xx, indnr=i), future.seed=TRUE)
    
    dff <- apply(df, 2, function(y)   {
      
      dff <- data.frame(order=y$orderind, id=indNames(x)[y$orderind], pop=pop(x)[y$orderind], nall=cumsum(y$nalltot), nallperc =  round(cumsum(y$nalltot)/sum(y$nalltot),3) )
      return(dff)
      
    })
    tabs <- lapply(dff, function(x)  table(x$pop[x$nallperc < percent]))
    tabs2 <- do.call(rbind, tabs)
    if (plot) {
      boxplot(tabs2, main="Number of individuals per population to retain 95% of alleles", ylab="Number of individuals", xlab="Population")
    }
    
    df <- dff
    
  }
  
  
  return(df)
  
}
```

## W06 Management of Small Populations {.unnumbered}


![](images/diana.png){.class width="200" height="200"} ![](images/peter.png){.class width="200" height="200"}


## Managing small populations: genetics and conservation


### Prerequisites
Small and fragmented populations are one of the most common challenges in conservation biology. Habitat loss and landscape fragmentation frequently interrupt natural gene flow, leaving species divided into small isolated populations. In such populations, evolutionary processes such as **genetic drift and inbreeding** become dominant forces, often leading to reduced genetic diversity, inbreeding depression, and ultimately increased extinction risk.
>>>>>>> main

Modern conservation management therefore increasingly incorporates **genetic information** to diagnose population fragmentation, evaluate genetic erosion, and design interventions that restore gene flow. One important strategy is **genetic rescue**, the deliberate increase of gene flow between populations to reduce inbreeding and restore genetic diversity.

In this session we introduce the genetic processes affecting small populations and outline a practical framework used by conservation geneticists to assess whether populations are genetically threatened and when interventions such as assisted gene flow may be appropriate. The tutorial component will demonstrate how genomic data can be used to diagnose fragmentation, estimate genetic diversity, and support management decisions.

## Learning outcomes

By the end of this session you should be able to:

-   explain why **small and isolated populations** are particularly vulnerable to genetic drift and inbreeding
-   describe how **habitat fragmentation disrupts gene flow**
-   recognise the genetic consequences of small population size, including **loss of diversity and inbreeding depression**
-   outline the concept of **genetic rescue** and when it may be beneficial
-   interpret basic genetic analyses used to diagnose **genetic erosion and population structure**
-   understand how genomic data can support **evidence-based conservation management**

## Session summary

Human-driven habitat fragmentation has created many small and isolated populations across the globe. In these populations, genetic drift increases inbreeding and reduces genetic diversity, limiting adaptive potential and increasing extinction risk.

Conservation genetics provides tools to diagnose these problems and guide management responses. A key approach is **genetic rescue**, which restores gene flow between populations to alleviate inbreeding depression and increase genetic diversity. Although risks such as outbreeding depression must be considered, evidence shows that genetic rescue is often highly beneficial when populations are small and isolated.

Effective genetic management therefore requires a structured process:\
1. **Diagnose genetic erosion** using genetic diversity, inbreeding, and population structure.\
2. **Evaluate potential donor populations** for increasing gene flow.\
3. **Assess risks such as outbreeding depression.**\
4. **Implement and monitor genetic management actions.**

Genomic data combined with clear decision frameworks allow conservation practitioners to make informed management decisions that increase the long-term viability of threatened populations.

## Worked Example

**Required packges**

```{r}
library(dartRverse)
library(future)
library(future.apply)

```

**Step 1: Read the data**

```{r}
#read the data
gl <- readRDS("data/mog.adspersa.dartr.rdata")
```

**Step 2: Select the relevant predefined samples**

```{r}
index <- gl@other$ind.metrics$mdb_mix =="Darling"
gl <- gl[ index, ]
```

**Step 3: Filter the data**

```{r}
#first eliminate monomorphs
gl <- gl.filter.monomorphs(gl, verbose=3)

#filter loci callrate (individuals with low call rates have already been removed)
gl <- gl.filter.callrate(gl, method = "loc", threshold=0.95, verbose=3)

#to visualise the frequency of rare alleles
gl.sfs(gl, singlepop = T)

#Filter rare alleles, a value of three removes any alleles present in only one or two individuals
gl <- gl.filter.maf(gl, threshold = 3, v=3)
```

**Step 4: Run and export the mixing results, this versions takes the "optimal" individual first, note that ncores may need to be adjusted to the number of cores you have available on your computer, I normally choose N-1**

***On this Posit Cloud we only have 2 cores, PLEASE DON'T CHANGE THE NUMBER OF CORES***

```{r}
system.time(yy <- gl.opt.ind.all(gl, ncores=2, first="optimal", plot = T))
write.csv(yy, file="mog.test1a.csv", row.names=F)
```

### Re-run the code, this time evening samples sizes per population to 14

**Read the data, select the relevant predefined samples**

```{r}
gl <- readRDS("data/mog.adspersa.dartr.rdata")
index <- gl@other$ind.metrics$mdb_mix =="Darling"
gl <- gl[ index, ]
```

**Reduces each population to the n= value with no replacement**

```{r}
gl <- gl.subsample.ind2 (gl, n = 14, replace = FALSE)
gl <- gl.filter.monomorphs(gl, v=3)
gl <- gl.filter.callrate(gl, method = "loc", threshold=0.95, verbose=3)
gl <- gl.filter.maf(gl, threshold = 3, verbose=3)
system.time(yy <- gl.opt.ind.all(gl, ncores=4, first="optimal", plot = T))
write.csv(yy, file="mog.test2a.csv", row.names=F)
```
